Odessa, the burnt bread isn't the end of the world. Honestly, Pip eats the burnt ones on purpose because he says they taste like campfire. Throw another batch in, we've got plenty of flour.
Wren, you can absolutely watch even though you've never played the game. Half the fun is just watching me panic about doors. I'll explain anything that doesn't make sense, just ask whenever.
Bram, you're home and you're safe, and that's what matters. I don't care that you came back without the sample. We'll get another one some other day, but there's only one of you.
Lantern, the stream isn't ending early, I'm just grabbing water. Two minutes, I promise, and I'll be right back to finish the raid defense. Keep an eye on the turrets for me while I'm gone.
Mara, I know you're worried about the new colonist, but she's harmless. She's quiet because she's shy, not because she's hiding something. Give her a few days and I bet you two will be friends.
Hey, Biscuit, it's okay that you missed the big raid. Honestly, you missed a lot of me yelling at turrets. I'll tell you the short version, and you'll be caught up in about a minute.
Nova, you don't need to apologize for the typo. We all knew what you meant, and honestly, the typo was funnier. Chat is a no judgment zone, especially for spelling.
Juno, the patient is stable now, you can step back. You did everything right, every single step of it. Go sit down, eat something, and let the medicine do its job for a while.
Pixel, the colony isn't doomed, I promise you. It looks bad because the power's out and it's dark, but it's just a solar flare. Everything comes back on in a day or so.
Everybody in the colony gets the day off tomorrow, no exceptions. It's been a hard week, three raids and a funeral, and they've earned some rest. We'll play games, eat a nice meal, and just breathe.

Chat, please welcome Juniper's friend, it's their very first stream. Say hi, be nice, and don't tell them about the vending machine yet. Let them discover the odd wing on their own, the way we all did.
Somebody give Hollis a hug for me, he's had the worst day. He lost the hunt, he lost his hat, and the deer chased him home again. I'd hug him myself if I could reach through the screen.
Everybody, go stretch and grab a snack while the colonists sleep. We've been at this for hours and your backs deserve a break. I'll keep the colony safe, and I'll be right here when you get back.
Tamsin, go sit with Rook by the fire tonight. He's been sad since the expedition and he won't say why. You're the one he talks to, so maybe he'll open up to you.
Chat, drop a heart for Juno, she just saved three people in one night. Three surgeries, back to back, no mistakes. She deserves every single heart you've got, and probably a vacation too.
Mara, take the extra blanket from the storeroom tonight. It's going to be freezing, and you always get cold first. Don't argue, just take it, the colony needs you warm.
Everybody say goodnight to Wren, they're heading off to bed. Thanks for hanging out all evening, Wren, it was lovely having you. Sleep well, and we'll see you next stream.
Pip, go show Odessa the new rock you found, she's been asking about it. She pretends she doesn't care about your rocks, but she totally does. Go on, she's in the kitchen.
Chat, please keep sending ideas for the new rec room. I love reading them, even the ridiculous ones, especially the ridiculous ones. We'll pick a winner at the end of the stream.
Juniper, go drink some water, you've been typing nonstop for an hour. I appreciate the energy, truly, but your body needs a break. The colony will still be here when you're back.
Can we all take a second to appreciate how far this colony's come? We started with a tent and a fire, and now there's a hospital and a cat with a desk. Isn't that kind of amazing?
Lantern, do you remember the very first night of this colony? You were the only one in chat and we talked for two hours about the freezer. Would you believe how many of us there are now?
Hey, Moss, did your colony make it through the winter? You were so worried about it last week, and I've been thinking about it. Did the heaters hold up like we planned?
Is it okay if we have a slow stream tonight? I'm a little tired, and the colony could use some quiet building time anyway. Just us, some walls, and the cat, if that sounds good to you.
Biscuit, did you finally get your own cat like you said you would? You talked about it for weeks, and I need an update. Is it orange, like Socks, please say it's orange?
Would you all mind if I named the new colonist after chat? Not anyone specific, just Chat, as a first name. I feel like you've earned a spot in the colony at this point, haven't you?
Static Fern, are you feeling any better than last stream? You mentioned you were sick, and I've been hoping you got some rest. Did the soup recipe help at all?
Cobalt, are you still here at three in the morning? You've been with us since the start of the stream, which was six hours ago. Do you want me to tell you a bedtime story about the gate?

Every time someone new shows up and asks what's going on, somebody in chat answers before I can. You explain the gate, the company, the cat, all of it. That kind of kindness makes this place feel like home.
Scar just sat down next to Tamsin at the grave and didn't say anything at all. She just sat there, shoulder to shoulder, for the rest of the evening. Sometimes that's all anyone needs, honestly.
Here's my thank you for this month, and it's a big one. You all showed up for every stream, even the boring ones and the late ones. This colony is ours because of you, and I'm really grateful.
Nova just shared a drawing of the colony, with all the colonists and the cat. I'm putting it up on screen right now so everyone can see it. It's beautiful, and I'm keeping it forever.

Mara and Odessa started cooking together every morning. Neither of them asked, they just showed up at the same stove and made it work. Now breakfast is twice as good and the kitchen is full of humming.

Pixel told me this stream helped them through a hard month, and I don't really know what to say. I'm just a girl yelling about doors in a strange video game. Thank you for letting us be part of your month.
Rook built a tiny bed for Socks right next to his own. It's got a pillow and a blanket and everything. She still sleeps on his chest every night, but she appreciates the gesture, I'm sure.
You know what, this colony has been through a lot, but tonight feels peaceful. The crew is fed, the gate is quiet, and chat is full of kind people. I'm just going to enjoy it for a minute.

Juniper and Moss have started a little tradition of greeting every new person in chat with a fact about the cat. It's adorable, and the facts are getting more ridiculous every week. I love you all for this.
Ivy wrote a little note and left it on Juno's desk. It just says thank you for fixing me. Juno read it and then sat quietly for a long time. This crew is going to make me cry on stream, honestly.
To everyone who stayed through the whole stream tonight, thank you. It was a long one, and we lost a lot, but we also built something. I'm really glad I didn't have to do it alone.
Hollis brushed the muffalo calf for an hour tonight, just like he used to do with Pudding. I think it's his way of keeping her memory around. It's honestly the sweetest thing in the whole colony.

Scar, take the north path to the ruins and stay off the main road. The raiders have been camping near the bridge all week. And I don't want a fight before you reach the site. Check in by radio at noon, and if anything looks wrong, turn around and come straight home.

Pip, I need the stockpile sorted before the trader arrives this afternoon. Steel on the left shelf, cloth in the middle. And all of your rocks in the box by the door where they can't trip anyone. Then grab some lunch, because you've been hauling since breakfast without a single break.

Chat, give me your best guess for how many days until the next raid. Whoever lands closest gets their name written on the new wall in the dining room. Type a number, just a number. And I'll lock the guesses in two minutes from now.

Mara, swap the rifle for the shotgun before you go into the odd wing. The hallways in there are tight and short. And a long gun is just going to slow you down around the corners. Take extra shells, too, and keep the flashlight on your belt where you can reach it.

Ivy, go plant the corn in the east field while the weather's still warm. We have maybe ten days before the frost comes in. And corn grows fast enough to make it if we start today. Leave the potatoes for now, we'll deal with those next season.

Everybody, gather in the dining hall for a quick colony meeting. I want to go over the plan for the expedition, who's going, who's staying. And who's on the night watch. It'll take five minutes, then you can all go back to whatever you were doing.

Hollis, set up the traps along the south fence before sundown. Wolves have been sniffing around the barn for two nights now, and I'd rather catch them before they catch the calf. Put a light by the gate, too. So the night watch can see the whole fence line.

Bram, finish the research on the new heaters before you start another sculpture. I know art is fun, but we're going into winter with old heaters that barely warm a single room. Get it done today. And I promise you can carve whatever you want tomorrow.

Rook, run the night watch from the roof tonight instead of the gate. You'll see more from up there, and whatever's been circling the colony won't expect anyone above it. Bring a thermos and a coat, it gets windy after midnight.

Tamsin, start harvesting the rice now, even though it's a day early. There's a cold front coming in tomorrow and I'd rather lose a little yield than the whole crop. Haul it straight to the freezer as you go.

Juno, set up a second bed in the hospital before the expedition leaves. I have a feeling somebody's coming back hurt, because somebody always does. Stock it with medicine and a clean blanket, just in case.

Odessa, cook simple meals for the next few days instead of the fancy ones. We need to stretch the food until the caravan comes back. Nobody's going to complain about plain soup if it means we don't run out.

Chat, help me pick the next research project, because I honestly can't decide. Option one is better armor, option two is faster crops, and option three is the company's anomaly scanner. Vote in the next minute and I'll start whichever wins.
Pip, Rook, carry the injured raider to the prison cell instead of leaving her outside. We can patch her up and see if she wants to join us. We could use another pair of hands, and she seems tough.

Ivy, close every door between the gate room and the bedrooms before you head to bed. It's a long walk, I know, but it's the only thing keeping anything from wandering in at night. Double check the last one, it sticks.

Juniper asked if we're ever going to finish the ship. And honestly, I've been thinking about it. We've got most of the parts, the reactor's nearly done, and the colony's in a good spot. Should we go for the launch in the next few streams, or keep building here a while longer?

Has anybody figured out what the company's anomaly scanner actually does? I've had it sitting in the office for three streams and I'm afraid to turn it on. The manual just says use with caution, and there are no other pages. Should I just press the button and find out live?

Cobalt suggested we move the whole colony closer to the river for the fishing. It's a big job, we'd have to rebuild every wall and every bed from scratch. On the other hand, fish would solve our food problem for good. Is it worth tearing everything down for that?
Is the trader coming tomorrow or the day after? I wrote it down somewhere and now I can't find the note anywhere. If it's tomorrow, I need to move the silver tonight, so does anyone remember?

He's fast and he's lucky, but Pip gets distracted by every shiny thing he sees. Then again, the last shiny thing he found was jade. Should we send him on the next expedition, or is that a terrible idea?

Wren asked if the colonists can learn new skills just by watching each other. Sort of, they get a little bit of experience from teaching. Do you want me to set up a little school in the library and test it?
Can anyone in chat remember what room we put the extra medicine in? I'm looking at the stockpile and I see three packs, and I swear we had ten. Did somebody move them, or did the odd wing eat them?
Moss is asking if we should take on a prisoner from the last raid. She's got good shooting skills and she's not hurt too badly. Do we try to recruit her, or let her walk home?

Our old storage room is closer to the freezer, but it's tiny and the ceiling leaks. I keep going back and forth on it all stream. Do we build the new kitchen in there, or start fresh next to the dining hall?

A legendary rifle would make Scar unstoppable on the wall, honestly. It would also mean no new medicine for a month, and that scares me more than raiders. Is it really worth spending all our silver on one gun?
Static Fern wants to know if we've explored the whole odd wing yet. Not even close, we've mapped maybe a third of it. Want me to send a team out tonight and push a little deeper?

Last time I assigned the bedrooms, Bram ended up next to the generator, which he says is way too loud. Maybe it's time to give them a choice instead. Should I let the colonists pick their own rooms this time?
Did anybody catch what the company phone said when it rang at noon? I was busy with the raid and I only heard the last word, which was basement. Is that a hint, or is that a threat?
Biscuit asked if we can see the colony from the satellite view. We can, actually, and it looks tiny from up there. Do you want me to zoom all the way out for a second?

Nova asked me what my favorite room in the colony is. And I've been thinking about it all stream. The library is cozy, the hospital is useful, and the greenhouse smells nice in my imagination. Which one would you pick if you had to live in this place for a month?

Before the expedition leaves tomorrow, I want to hear from chat about the route. We can go through the forest, which is slow but safe, or along the river, which is fast but full of wolves. What would you choose if it were your colonists walking that road?

Pixel's asking which colonist I'd send on a solo mission if I absolutely had to. Scar has the skills, Hollis has the patience, and Ivy has the luck, apparently. Who would you trust to come back alone from the deep rooms?
Here's a question I've been chewing on since last stream. If the company built the gate, why do they need us to explore it at all? What are they not telling us about what's on the other side?
We just found a locked chest in the odd wing with no key anywhere nearby. It's heavy, it rattles a little, and it's warm to the touch. What do you think is inside, chat?

Lantern asked how many colonists I'm aiming for in the long run. Honestly, I think ten is the sweet spot, enough to run everything, small enough to keep fed. How many do you usually keep in your own colonies?

With winter coming, which crop should we plant in the greenhouse first? Rice grows fast, corn lasts longer, and berries make everybody a little happier. Where should I spend the space, chat, since we only have room for one?
Juniper asked where the company headquarters is on the map, and that's a great question. It's not on the map at all, actually, it only shows up on the contracts. Where do you think it really is?
When the gate opens next, who should go through first? Scar is the obvious answer, but she's been on every mission and she's tired. Who else do you think is ready?
Moss wants to know what happens if we ignore a company contract. I've never tried, honestly, I'm a little scared to find out. What's the worst they could do to us?
How should we spend the bonus silver from the last contract? I'm thinking a new freezer and better beds, but chat might have better ideas. What would make this colony feel more like home?
Cobalt asked which mod I'd recommend for someone starting out. Honestly, play the base game first and learn how everything works. Which one did you start with, if you play?
She walked out of the forest with no gear, no name tag, and a company badge pinned to her coat. Something doesn't add up here at all. Where do you think the new colonist really came from?

Hmm, I think I left the back door open again last night. That would explain why the squirrel was in the kitchen this morning eating the bread. Closing it now, and leaving a note for future me on the wall.

Wait, did I already send the samples, or did I just think about sending them? I remember packing the box, and I remember labeling it, but I don't remember the courier. Let me check the quest log real quick.

Right, the turret needs a power line, I forgot that part. No wonder it hasn't fired at anything in two days. It's been sitting there looking tough and doing nothing, like a guard dog made of cardboard.
Reminder to myself, the heater in the barn is on the wrong setting. The calf has been sleeping in a sauna for a week. Turning it down now, sorry, little one.
Hold on, the bedroom wall is one tile short. I can see the snow coming through the gap from up here. That's going to be a cold night for Rook if I don't fix it.
Huh, the stockpile says we've twelve hats. We have six colonists, and none of them wear two at once, except Bram. I'm not going to ask why, I'm just going to accept that we're a hat colony now.
Let me just pause the game for a second and think this through. If the raid comes from the north, the turrets are useless. Maybe I move one of them to the barn before it starts.
Honestly, I should have built the hospital closer to the gate. Every time someone gets hurt in the odd wing, they have to limp across the entire map. Next colony, hospital first, gate second.
Alright, mental note, Ivy is allergic to the strange berries from the odd wing. She sneezed for an hour after eating one. I'm marking those berries as do not eat.
